The statement and proof were compared with 926bac9f38574135: only provenance and the now accepted ordinary-rigidity dependency changed. The contradiction quantifiers are correct: failure for rho=1/k forces D(B_k)<Gamma+alpha e_k/V_k, because an ordinary deepest point reaching that own-body bound would pay all endpoint configurations. A positive deepest point is interior, so the claimed interior-center conclusion causes no loss. A maximum-volume inscribed simplex exists by compactness of the vertex tuples. Sending it to the standard simplex bounds every barycentric coordinate of B_k in absolute value by one, hence gives a compact normalized family. Each subsequential limit is a simplex by ordinary rigidity; maximality persists through approximation of its vertices and forces that limit to equal the fixed inscribed simplex. They are bookkeeping changes for independently quantified tilts, not unauthorized transformations of an actual mixed source. After these translations, C_j lies in 2B and A_j in 2(B-B). Thus all partners lie in a dimension-dependent compact set and their volumes remain uniformly positive. If a uniform large-inscribed-simplex conclusion failed for growing families, selecting one offending partner per family gives a convergent full-dimensional subsequence; ordinary rigidity turns its limit into a simplex of volume at least the middle limit volume. Approximating its vertices contradicts failure. No bound on the number of partners is needed. The centered determinant estimate replaces a row with largest maximum by the all-ones row. After centering the other rows, its product is bounded by r_J^(N-J+1), since rows J through N contribute precisely q=N-J+1 factors and all other row maxima are at most one. Since q>N/2, delta_0=N^(-N/(2q))-1/N is positive. The stated uniform volume-ratio threshold indeed forces at least J support coordinates above b+delta. The facet credits are measurable fixed subsets selected before moving the center. Their total coordinate average is at least J e/N. The support margin uses the original large partner, which contains its approximating simplex, so replacing the simplex by the partner can only improve the credit. The homothetic partner-cap estimate holds for every real tilt and closed cap; either the partner already pays the full small-endpoint volume or the small endpoint threshold lies below the displayed credited threshold. The perturbation margin delta-2sigma-3r-6R epsilon is valid with the common body bound and r<=1. The individual r_j tend to zero uniformly because each a_j<=e and each c_j>=V/(1+1/k). The barycentric-gradient displacement equation has exactly one solution, because its right-hand sides sum to zero and the gradients have precisely their single sum-zero dependence. Its norm is at most sqrt(d)e/(N Gamma V), so the point is eventually interior and all credited margins survive. For full-dimensional Hausdorff limits and proper section planes, section bodies converge after plane identification: move a limiting section point toward a section point interior to the limiting body, then adjust slightly to the moving plane. This gives the lower inclusion; boundedness gives the upper inclusion. Convex section-volume continuity and a compact proper-plane family yield the required uniform coarea-density estimate. The exact Grunbaum baseline is used at the true centroid g_k, rather than replacing its cap volume by a limiting simplex volume. Integrating the small coarea error only over the displacement interval of length O(e/V) makes the entire error O(e). The displayed choice zeta K_d(sqrt(d)+1)+N Gamma K_d epsilon<=zeta_0 gives precisely the claimed zeta_0 e loss, including the normal perturbation term. In each canonical normal neighborhood the resulting mass is Gamma V+(J/N-zeta_0)e, strictly greater than Gamma V+alpha e. Outside fixed neighborhoods, classical simplex equality identifies no further equality normals; compactness gives a strictly positive ordinary centroid cap gap. Uniform body and center convergence preserve this gap and it dominates alpha e/V as that ratio tends to zero. All nonzero continuous normals are covered after positive normalization; affine constants cancel and arbitrary tilts scale together. A subsequent shrinkage of rho imposes Gamma+alpha rho<1, making every purely integer containing cap payable by the whole middle fiber. In an actual source, distinct endpoint fibers remain necessary to sum the pair masses. The argument proves existence of a dimension-dependent rho only. It does not provide a uniform-in-d threshold, a quantitative stability modulus, or a global low-target parity repair. The stated limitations are essential.
